newsitem.title: USA: US money managers flat on US debt positions-survey.
newsitem.headline: US money managers flat on US debt positions-survey.

text.p: Money managers' duration exposure in U.S. debt markets were flat over the past week, apparently intent on beginning 1997 with a clean slate, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.

"Overall, money managers in the survey are flat, however, some of the larger portfolios ended the year marginally short," the report said. In the week ended December 31, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading advanced to 5.10 from 5.04 in the prior week. The asset-weighted number rose to 5.27 from 5.26 in the week ended December 24.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating that investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio dropped to 6.56 percent from 6.60 percent.
Duration bogey held steady at 4.22 on an arithmetic basis and 4.93 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Eight percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, no change from the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active slipped to 5.0 from 6.0 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
